name: Masahati
subtitle: A workspace for the spaces we work in.
description: A platform for managing study and coworking spaces: rooms, visits, bookings, checkout, and day-to-day operations.
highlights: Building owner, staff, customer, and platform workflows with Django templates and HTMX.
Connecting seating, timed visits, bookings, checkout, and cash review to PostgreSQL-backed business logic.
Developing the product's interface alongside permission checks, operation tracking, and automated workflow tests.
note: An ongoing product. The image is a design preview using fictional demonstration data. Production hosting is still being prepared.

name: HealthGuard
subtitle: Selected text. Structured analysis.
description: A Chrome extension that captures selected medical claims from webpages and sends them to a Python analysis API.
highlights: Developed a Manifest V3 extension with content scripts, a background worker, and a React popup.
Integrated a Flask REST API with optional facebook/bart-large-mnli zero-shot classification and a rule-based fallback.
Implemented selection, loading, result, and error states, and documented the frontend-backend API contract.
note: Educational prototype with an optional inference service and a mock fallback. It is not a clinically validated medical fact-checking system.

name: PUBG Language Transpiler and Web IDE
subtitle: A language, from tokens to execution.
description: A custom-language transpiler and web IDE that makes the compilation pipeline visible, from tokenization to generated Python.
highlights: Built a tokenizer, parser, semantic analyzer, and code generator covering eight language constructs.
Implemented symbol-table-based analysis with six categories of static checks, including type checking and undeclared identifiers.
Designed a React/Vite IDE with dedicated views for compiler stages, output, and errors.
note: Custom language and an interactive web IDE. The repository link opens the final implementation branch.

name: AI Search and Game Algorithm Projects
subtitle: Different paths. Better decisions.
description: Pathfinding and game-playing projects exploring how search strategies navigate a space and choose a move.
highlights: Applied Greedy Best-First Search, A*, Hill Climbing, and a Genetic Algorithm to pathfinding.
Developed a Minimax Tic-Tac-Toe AI with three difficulty levels.
note: Experiments in contrasting search strategies and choosing moves in adversarial games.

name: College Attendance System
subtitle: Identity at the heart of the application.
description: An attendance-application foundation with account management and Identity workflows.
highlights: Implemented Identity flows including registration, email confirmation, password reset, and two-factor authentication.
Used ASP.NET Core MVC, Entity Framework Core, and SQL Server LocalDB.
Applied HTTPS redirection, exception handling, and HSTS, with responsive Razor Pages and Bootstrap.
note: Identity and account workflows form the application foundation. The repository includes the local setup.

name: Librarium
subtitle: The complete borrowing journey.
description: A library management application with member and admin roles, catalog search, filtering, and borrowing workflows.
highlights: Built member and admin workflows with hashed-password authentication and protected routes.
Implemented catalog search and filtering, borrowing and returns, loan history, and due dates.
Packaged the application with Docker Compose and documented the system with ERD, DFD, and sequence diagrams.
note: Academic project. Local setup is documented in the repository; a persistent hosted database is still needed for a durable public deployment.

name: MiniFAT Virtual File System Shell
subtitle: A small disk. A complete set of ideas.
description: A 1 MB virtual FAT file system in Python, exposed through a 13-command interactive shell.
highlights: Implemented a virtual file system backed by a 1 MB virtual disk.
Built a 13-command interactive shell for working with the virtual file system.
note: Systems project retained from the original CV. It is an interactive shell rather than a hosted web application.
